text:
Ivan (customer): Hey team — saw a 3x spike on invoice 2026-03-01 for streaming calls. We're pretty sure it's from our web client cancelling mid-gen then auto-reconnecting. Example request-id: rq_8f3b2c. Logs attached: `sse-close event` then quick reconnect within 200ms. Can you check if tokens were double-counted?
Tara (support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact SSE frames you saw (headers + first/last event ids)? Also did the client send any resume header like `Last-Event-ID`? :eyes:
Ivan (customer): Here's a snippet — client sends: `GET /v1/responses/stream` with `Accept: text/event-stream` then `x-client-resume: resume_9a` on reconnect. Server replies: `event: chunk
data: {...partial...}
` then `event: final
data: {...}`. On reconnect we see same final payload again, but with different `connection-id`.
Tara (support): Thanks. Can you confirm if your client increments a local seq when reconnecting? We need to know whether the retry is semantic (resend last tokens) or a resumed stream.
Nate (infra): Quick check from our side — I pulled the ledger for `rq_8f3b2c`. We have two close cases: one closed at 15:02:12 with final token delta 1,024, then another close at 15:02:13 for the same logical request id but different connection id. Looks like the edge retried the final event after a timeout while the runtime was finalizing the KV cache. Possibly a replay because there was no idempotency key at the LB layer.
Maria (billing): If the runtime emitted two finalize events both incrementing the invoice ledger, that would create the spike. We can block a provisional credit but need a deterministic way to dedupe before adjusting invoices.
Nate (infra): Repro steps I recommend: 1) Start a streaming generation with a long-running finalization (simulate by delaying finalize by 150ms). 2) Kill client connection and immediately reconnect with `x-client-resume` header. 3) Observe two `final` events emitted. I can share a small curl script: 
```bash
# simulate reconnect
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' "$API/responses/stream?request_id=rq_8f3b2c" # get partials then ctrl-c
# immediately reconnect with resume header
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'x-client-resume: resume_9a' "$API/responses/stream?request_id=rq_8f3b2c"
```
Tara (support): Good clear repro, Nate. Short-term workaround for customers: set the client to wait 500ms before reconnecting or include an idempotency header so LB doesn't replay the final chunk. We'll document this in the KB. :memo:
Maria (billing): For this invoice (2026-03-01) please create a billing ticket referencing `rq_8f3b2c` and hold a provisional credit of the duplicated token amount (1,024 tokens). I'll need the ledger ids and evidence of duplicate finalize events.
Nate (infra): I'll dump the internal trace and ledger ids to the support ticket. Root cause hypothesis: race between finalize ack and LB retry path causing duplicated finalize delta; longer-term fix is to make finalize operation idempotent at the ledger level (check if finalize already applied for given request id/kv-hash).
Ivan (customer): Thanks — that'll help. Any ETA on the fix? The client can't pause reconnects for too long.
Nate (infra): Short-term ETA: docs + rollback prevention (500ms client wait suggestion) within 24h. Mid-term (idempotent finalize) is an engineering ticket with ~2-week SLA to rollout to edge and runtime. I'll link the PR when created. :+1:
DeployBot: Deployment started for `support/fix/idempotent-finalize` to staging at 2026-03-17T16:28Z.
Tara (support): I'll follow up in the support ticket with the KB steps and mark this thread for billing reconciliation. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
